questions.question: What is log aggregation?

options.text: Collecting logs from multiple sources into a centralized system for search and analysis

questions.explanation: Log aggregation: collect logs from all services/servers into one place. Enables: searching across systems, correlation, alerting, long-term storage. Essential for distributed systems. Examples: ELK Stack, Splunk, Datadog.

questions.question: What is the ELK Stack?

options.text: Elasticsearch (search), Logstash (processing), Kibana (visualization) for log management

questions.explanation: ELK Stack: Elasticsearch (store and search logs), Logstash (collect and transform), Kibana (visualize and dashboard). Now often EFK (Fluentd instead of Logstash) or Elastic Stack. Popular open-source solution.

questions.question: Why is centralized logging important for microservices?

options.text: Requests span multiple services; need to trace and correlate logs across all of them

questions.explanation: Microservices logging challenge: one request touches many services. Without centralized logging, must SSH into each server. Centralized: search all logs, correlate by request ID, see full picture.

questions.question: What is a log shipper?

options.text: An agent that collects logs from sources and sends them to the aggregation system

questions.explanation: Log shipper: agent on each server collecting logs. Examples: Filebeat, Fluentd, Fluent Bit, Logstash. Reads log files, adds metadata, buffers, ships to central system. Lightweight, reliable delivery.

questions.question: What is structured logging?

options.text: Logging in a consistent, parseable format (JSON) with defined fields instead of free-form text

questions.explanation: Structured logging: {"timestamp": "...", "level": "ERROR", "service": "auth", "user_id": 123, "message": "..."}. Enables: filtering, aggregation, alerting on specific fields. Much better than parsing free-form text.

questions.question: What is log retention and why does it matter?

options.text: How long logs are stored; balances storage costs, compliance requirements, and debugging needs

questions.explanation: Log retention: how long to keep logs. Considerations: storage cost (logs are big), compliance (some require years), debugging (need recent logs), legal (discovery requirements). Tiered: hot (recent), warm, cold (archive).

questions.question: What is the difference between Logstash and Fluentd?

options.text: Both are log processors; Logstash (Ruby, more plugins) vs Fluentd (C/Ruby, lighter, CNCF project)

questions.explanation: Logstash: Elastic's processor, rich plugins, higher resource usage. Fluentd: CNCF project, lighter (Fluent Bit even lighter), Kubernetes-native. Both: collect, transform, route logs. Choose based on ecosystem.

questions.question: What is log sampling?

options.text: Collecting only a percentage of logs to reduce volume and cost while maintaining visibility

questions.explanation: Log sampling: at high volume, store subset (e.g., 10%). Reduces cost, still provides visibility. Strategies: random sampling, sample by importance (always keep errors), head-based sampling. Tradeoff: might miss rare events.

questions.question: What is Splunk?

options.text: A commercial platform for log management, search, analysis, and visualization

questions.explanation: Splunk: enterprise log management platform. Features: powerful search (SPL), dashboards, alerting, ML capabilities. Expensive but feature-rich. Alternatives: ELK (open source), Datadog, Sumo Logic.

questions.question: What is the challenge of logging in containerized environments?

options.text: Containers are ephemeral; logs must be collected before container dies, stdout/stderr handling

questions.explanation: Container logging challenges: containers die (logs lost), many containers (scale), stdout/stderr (not files), dynamic IPs. Solutions: log to stdout, DaemonSet collectors (Fluentd), sidecar pattern, container runtime integration.

questions.question: What is log parsing?

options.text: Extracting structured fields from log messages for indexing and querying

questions.explanation: Log parsing: extract fields from log lines. '192.168.1.1 - - [10/Oct/2024:13:55:36] "GET /api"' → {ip: '192.168.1.1', timestamp: '...', method: 'GET', path: '/api'}. Enables filtering, aggregation. Grok patterns common.

questions.question: A company has 500 microservices generating 10TB of logs daily. What's the logging strategy?

options.text: Centralized aggregation with structured logging, sampling for high-volume services, tiered retention

questions.explanation: 500 services, 10TB/day: centralized aggregation essential (ELK, Splunk, Datadog). Structured logging for queryability. Sample high-volume/low-value logs. Tiered retention (7 days hot, 30 days warm, archive cold). Cost management critical.
